title: Salmonella Outbreak Linked to Jalapeño Peppers from Chipotle and Qdoba
excerpt: Hundreds of people in at least 27 states have been sickened by the bacteria in the latest food-linked outbreak.
content_html:
A Salmonella outbreak linked to jalapeño peppers has sickened hundreds of people in at least 27 U.S. states, according to an Aug. 6 food-safety alert released by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

The CDC identified jalapeño peppers grown in Sinaloa, Mexico, and distributed by Coast Citrus Distributors as the source of the outbreak. The peppers were served at restaurants including Chipotle and Qdoba, the CDC said. At least 345 people have been sickened in the outbreak to date, and 36 people have been hospitalized. 

Minnesota and Colorado have been especially hard-hit, reporting at least 110 cases each. A woman in Minnesota has sued Chipotle claiming that the restaurant allegedly served her contaminated jalapeño peppers. Kristen Behne says she developed a 102°F fever and was hospitalized with sepsis after eating a chicken burrito bowl at a Chipotle restaurant in Roseville, Minn., in late June, CBS News reported.

Chipotle said in an Aug. 5 statement that it had removed jalapeños supplied by Coast Citrus Distributors from its restaurants across the country “and replaced them with product from different growers.” Qdoba said it had removed all jalapeños from its restaurants “out of an abundance of caution.” 

The CDC and U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) said in an update about the outbreak that they do not “consider there to be a current ongoing risk” linked to Chipotle or Qdoba. The CDC and FDA said they continue to investigate the outbreak, including probing whether the contaminated jalapeño peppers were sold at grocery stores.

The FDA said Coast Citrus Distributors has agreed to initiate a recall of jalapeño peppers implicated in the outbreak and was “in the process of identifying and contacting affected customers.”

Salmonella, a bacteria that mostly spreads through contaminated food and water, is one of the most common foodborne pathogens in the U.S. and globally, infecting tens of millions of people every year. Incidences of the disease are on the rise globally, according to a 2025 study. Salmonella cases increased by almost 50% between 1990 and 2021, and deaths from Salmonella infection increased by almost 27% over the same period, the study said.  

Most people infected with Salmonella suffer diarrhea, fever, and stomach cramps, starting 6 hours to 6 days after ingesting the bacteria, the CDC says. Most people recover without treatment after 4 to 7 days, but the illness can be severe or even life-threatening in some people, including young children, the elderly, and people with weak immune systems. 

The CDC recommends people seek medical care if they have severe or lingering symptoms of food poisoning, including a fever higher than 102°F; diarrhea that doesn’t improve after 3 days; bloody diarrhea; and signs of dehydration, such as a lack of urination. 

U.S. health officials are currently investigating multiple Salmonella outbreaks across the country, including one linked to eggs and another tied to backyard poultry. The FDA said in late July that Midwest Poultry Services had recalled 1.5 million eggs due to possible Salmonella contamination. Affected eggs had been sold at Kroger stores in Texas and Louisiana; Brookshire Grocery stores in Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, and Louisiana; as well as other retailers in those states and in Mississippi and New Mexico.

The U.S. is also grappling with a record cyclosporiasis outbreak that has sickened thousands of people. Michigan health officials said on Aug. 3 that two people had died in the outbreak.

content_html_zh:
根据美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 8 月 6 日发布的食品安全警报，与墨西哥辣椒有关的沙门氏菌疫情已导致美国至少 27 个州数百人患病。

疾病预防控制中心确定墨西哥锡那罗亚州种植并由海岸柑橘经销商分销的墨西哥辣椒是此次疫情的源头。 疾病预防控制中心表示，Chipotle 和 Qdoba 等餐厅都供应这些辣椒。 迄今为止，疫情已造成至少 345 人患病，36 人住院治疗。

明尼苏达州和科罗拉多州受到的打击尤其严重，各报告至少 110 例病例。 明尼苏达州的一名妇女起诉 Chipotle，声称该餐厅涉嫌为她提供受污染的墨西哥辣椒。 据哥伦比亚广播公司新闻报道，克里斯汀·贝尼 (Kristen Behne) 表示，6 月下旬，她在明尼苏达州罗斯维尔的一家 Chipotle 餐厅吃了一碗鸡肉卷饼后，发烧了 102 华氏度，并因败血症入院治疗。

Chipotle 在 8 月 5 日的一份声明中表示，该公司已从其全国各地的餐厅中撤掉了 Coast Citrus Distributors 提供的墨西哥辣椒，“并用来自不同种植者的产品取而代之”。 Qdoba 表示，“出于谨慎考虑”，该公司已将所有墨西哥辣椒从其餐厅中撤下。

美国疾病控制和预防中心 (CDC) 和美国食品和药物管理局 (FDA) 在有关疫情的最新消息中表示，他们“认为目前不存在与 Chipotle 或 Qdoba 有关的持续风险”。 疾病预防控制中心和食品和药物管理局表示，他们将继续调查疫情，包括调查杂货店是否出售受污染的墨西哥辣椒。

FDA 表示，海岸柑橘经销商已同意启动对与疫情有关的墨西哥辣椒的召回，并且“正在识别和联系受影响的客户”。

沙门氏菌是一种主要通过受污染的食物和水传播的细菌，是美国和全球最常见的食源性病原体之一，每年感染数千万人。 根据 2025 年的一项研究，这种疾病的发病率在全球范围内呈上升趋势。 研究称，1990 年至 2021 年间，沙门氏菌病例增加了近 50%，同期沙门氏菌感染死亡人数增加了近 27%。

CDC 表示，大多数感染沙门氏菌的人在摄入细菌后 6 小时到 6 天后会出现腹泻、发烧和胃痉挛的症状。 大多数人在 4 至 7 天后无需治疗即可康复，但对于某些人来说，这种疾病可能很严重，甚至危及生命，包括幼儿、老年人和免疫系统较弱的人。

CDC 建议人们如果出现严重或持续的食物中毒症状（包括发烧高于 102°F），请立即就医；腹泻3天后仍未改善；血性腹泻；以及脱水迹象，例如缺乏排尿。

美国卫生官员目前正在调查全国多起沙门氏菌疫情，其中一起与鸡蛋有关，另一起与后院家禽有关。 FDA 7 月下旬表示，由于可能受到沙门氏菌污染，中西部家禽服务中心召回了 150 万只鸡蛋。 受影响的鸡蛋曾在德克萨斯州和路易斯安那州的克罗格商店出售；德克萨斯州、俄克拉荷马州、阿肯色州和路易斯安那州的布鲁克郡杂货店；以及这些州以及密西西比州和新墨西哥州的其他零售商。

美国还在努力应对创纪录的环孢子虫病疫情，该病已导致数千人患病。 密歇根州卫生官员8月3日表示，已有两人在疫情中死亡。
